What kind of place is Denver for property tax purposes?

Denver is a consolidated city and county, so one government handles what a city and a county handle elsewhere. It consolidated as the City and County of Denver on December 1, 1902, and it is described as the only U.S. state capital that is a consolidated city-county.

Adams, Arapahoe and Jefferson counties surround it. The city covers about 154.7 square miles, sits at an official elevation of 5,280 feet, and was platted on November 17, 1858 at the meeting of Cherry Creek and the South Platte River. The 2020 census counted 715,522 residents, and the page gives a 2025 estimate of 740,613.

For a seller, the consolidation means one set of offices. The Assessor values your house, the Treasury Division bills the tax, and the Clerk and Recorder files your deed, all inside the same city government.

Which Denver neighborhoods and employers shape the housing market?

Denver has 78 official neighborhoods, and the Wikipedia article lists the City and County of Denver, Denver Public Schools, the State of Colorado, Denver Health and United Airlines as top 2023 employers.

Employer2023 employees
City and County of Denver13,584
Denver Public Schools12,693
State of Colorado10,686
Denver Health and Hospital Authority9,502
United Airlines7,230

Government, energy and mining, telecommunications and logistics are the sectors the article names.

What does Denver weather mean for a house?

Hail is the main weather risk the sources point to. Denver ranks tenth among U.S. cities of 50,000 or more for hailstorm exposure and has had three of the ten costliest hailstorms in the country.

The climate is cool and semi-arid with about 3,100 hours of sunshine a year and roughly 49 to 53 inches of snow. For owners, that points to roof age and condition as a recurring question. Roof age and condition are worth knowing before you talk to any buyer.

How is Denver property tax figured?

Taxes equal actual value minus a value reduction, times an assessment rate, times the mill levy. The Denver Assessor FAQ gives the 2024 figures in the table.

Property typeValue reduction per parcelAssessment rate
Residential$55,0006.7%
Commercial improved$30,00027.9%
All other$027.9%

Denver's combined general mill levy for 2024 was 79.202 mills, or 0.079202. Taxing authorities set levies in December, and levies and rates change from year to year, so treat these as 2024 numbers and look at your own bill.

Real property is reappraised every two years, in odd-numbered years. Residential values come from the market approach, using sales in the 24 months ending June 30 of the prior year.

When is Denver property tax due?

Half is due on the last day of February and half on June 15, or the whole amount by April 30. The Treasury's property tax calendar lays out the year.

  • January: annual tax statements are mailed.
  • April 1: deferral applications are due.
  • April 30: full payment due, and the elderly and disabled refund application deadline.
  • May through August: delinquency notices are mailed.
  • July 1: later delinquencies become available for tax lien buyers to endorse.
  • September and October: delinquent taxes are advertised in the local newspaper.
  • October: the real estate tax lien auction is held.

Denver also lists July 15 as the application date for senior and disabled veteran exemptions, and an April 15 date for personal property declarations. The calendar does not list penalty or interest rates, so ask Treasury for the payoff on any delinquent account.

How do you protest a Denver property value?

The protest deadline is June 8 each year, or the next business day if June 8 falls on a weekend or holiday. You can file in writing, in person or online with the instructions on your Notice of Valuation.

Include your reasons, evidence such as sales of similar homes or condition problems, your parcel or schedule number and a daytime phone number. If you disagree with the decision, you can go to the State Board of Assessment Appeals, to District Court, or to binding arbitration.

The Assessor also says you may protest up to two prior years' values that you did not protest at the time, using a Board of County Commissioners petition for abatement or refund of taxes.

Can seniors or active military defer Denver property tax?

Colorado runs a deferral program through the county treasurer, and applications run January 1 to April 1. The state treasury says it covers owners 65 or older and active-duty military who meet its rules.

For seniors, the page requires age 65 by December 31 of the year, residence at the property, prior taxes paid, liens and mortgages of no more than 75 percent of actual value, and no reverse mortgage. The deferral is a loan recorded as a junior lien, with interest running from May 1. A sale or contract of sale makes repayment due 90 days later.

Anyone selling a Denver house with a deferral on it should ask for the payoff early, so the title company can include it at closing. Active-duty military applicants have a different test: liens, mortgages and deferrals together must stay under 100 percent of actual value for VA-guaranteed loans, or 90 percent otherwise.

What happens if you sell a Denver house with property tax due?

The title company asks Treasury for the amount owed and pays it from your proceeds at closing. You do not have to find the money first.

The sooner the account is current, the fewer steps remain. An account that moved toward the October lien sale needs the lien buyer's payoff in addition to the tax. In that case, a title officer who knows Denver's process saves time.

If you owe back tax on a Denver house, are behind on payments or inherited it, we can send you a written cash offer for the house as it stands. You decide whether it works.

How do you get to and around Denver?

Denver International Airport is about 20 miles from downtown and serves as the city's official weather station. Wikipedia also notes that a commuter railway system began operating in the metro area in 2015.

The metro area has about 3.1 million residents, and its 2023 gross domestic product was $311.9 billion, the 18th largest among U.S. metro economies. Denver Public Schools alone employed about 12,700 people in 2023.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What are Denver service liens for storm drain and sewer?

Denver mails separate lien statements for storm drain and sanitary sewer service, and these can show up on a property alongside regular tax. The Treasury calendar says storm drain statements go out in February, April, June and August, and sanitary sewer statements in March, May, July and September.

If a seller has an unpaid service lien, the title company will find it in its search and list it as a payoff. Ask Treasury about the balance early.

For general city questions, Denver lists 3-1-1, or (720) 913-1311 from outside the city, as its main number.

Frequently asked questions

When is Denver property tax due?

The first half is due the last day of February, the second half June 15, and full payment April 30. Dates falling on a weekend or holiday move to the next business day.

What is the Denver property tax protest deadline?

June 8 each year, or the next business day. You can file in writing, in person or online per the Notice of Valuation.

What was Denver's mill levy in 2024?

The Assessor's FAQ gives a combined general mill levy of 79.202 mills for 2024. Levies are set each December, so use the figure on your current bill.

How often does Denver reappraise homes?

Every two years, in odd-numbered years. Residential values use only the market approach, based on sales in the 24 months ending June 30 of the prior year.

Does Denver run a tax lien sale?

Yes. Delinquent taxes are advertised in September and October, and the real estate tax lien auction is held in October, per the Treasury calendar.

Does selling a Denver house trigger the property tax deferral repayment?

Yes. A sale or contract of sale makes repayment due 90 days afterward under Colorado's deferral program.

Boulder, CO Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Colorado
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Boulder, CO Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Boulder, CO Property Tax Guide sale

Where is Boulder, and who bills property tax there?

Boulder is the county seat of Boulder County, set at the base of the Rocky Mountain foothills about 25 miles northwest of Denver. The Boulder County Treasurer bills and collects the tax, and the Boulder County Assessor sets the value.

The city does not run a separate property tax office. A Boulder homeowner gets one bill that adds up the levies of every taxing body on the parcel, such as the school district and local governments. The Treasurer's office is at 1325 Pearl St. in Boulder, and its phone is 303-441-3520.

The city has about 26 square miles of land and a 2025 Census estimate of 105,689 residents, down slightly from 108,250 in the 2020 count. Denver International Airport is roughly 33 miles east-southeast.

What does Boulder's history mean for a house there today?

Boulder began as a gold camp. Prospectors led by Thomas Aikins reached Boulder Canyon in late 1858, gold turned up along Boulder Creek in early 1859, and the town was incorporated on November 4, 1871.

The Colorado General Assembly chose Boulder for the University of Colorado in 1861, and the campus opened on September 5, 1877. Colorado became a state on August 1, 1876.

Older houses can carry deferred repairs. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is can skip the repair negotiations that often stall a conventional sale.

What do Census figures say about Boulder housing?

The Census Bureau shows that fewer than half of Boulder homes are owner-occupied,. These are the QuickFacts numbers for the city.

MeasureBoulder city
Population, 2020 Census108,250
Population estimate, July 1, 2025105,689
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020-202447.2%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024$1,039,500
Median gross rent, 2020-2024$2,018
Households, 2020-202444,432
Persons per household2.12
Median household income, 2020-2024$87,493

A median home value above $1 million means the tax bill is large in dollars even when the rate is modest. It also means a missed payment grows quickly, because the penalty is a percentage of the bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who are the major employers around Boulder?

The University of Colorado Boulder is the largest employer, followed by Ball Corporation. Wikipedia's 2022 employer list for the Boulder area gives these headcounts.

  • University of Colorado Boulder: 6,200
  • Ball Corporation: 4,800
  • Boulder Valley School District: 3,832
  • St. Vrain Valley School District: 3,570
  • Boulder Community Health: 2,360

The same source puts the metro area's 2022 economic output at $35.608 billion. Employers this large mean Boulder houses are often sold by people relocating for work.

How does Boulder's weather affect a house?

Boulder gets cold winters with chinook winds, warm summers with afternoon thunderstorms, and heavy water events now and then. Snowfall averages roughly 88 inches a season by the article's text, and annual precipitation is about 21.2 inches.

About 30 days a year reach 90 degrees or more. The record high is 104 degrees and the record low is minus 33. Roofs and heating systems carry real load here.

The September 2013 floods are the best-known example of water risk. Boulder recorded 9.08 inches of rain on September 12 alone, and Boulder Creek ran above 5,000 cubic feet per second against a normal 150 to 200. Boulder County had 262 homes destroyed and nearly 300 damaged. Ask the title company and your insurer about flood history on any parcel near a creek.

What do open space and transit mean for Boulder neighborhoods?

Boulder's greenbelt limits where new houses can go, which keeps existing ones in demand. The city's open space program traces back to 1899, and voters approved a dedicated open space sales tax in 1967. The Open Space and Mountain Parks department manages about 8,000 acres of forest west of town.

The Regional Transportation District runs the bus service, including the HOP, SKIP, JUMP and Flatiron Flyer routes, and US 36 links the city to Denver. Boulder has no rail line today. The proposed Northwest Rail Line would reach it only by 2044, funding permitting.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

When is Boulder property tax due, and what does a late payment cost?

For 2026 the Boulder County Treasurer lists two ways to pay: two half payments due March 2 and June 15, or one full payment due April 30. The county says there are no discounts for early payment.

Late interest is a percentage that depends on the month paid.

Month paidFirst halfFull paymentSecond half
March1%Not lateNot late
April2%Not lateNot late
May3%1%Not late
June 1 to 154%2%Not late
June 16 to 304%2%1%
July5%3%2%
August6%4%3%

For September through December, the county says to contact the office. Delinquent payments must be in certified funds, and so must any payment made after September 1. A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

How is the tax figured, and what rates apply?

Boulder County bills assessed value times the mill levy, and assessed value is actual value times an assessment rate. One mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value.

The county's calculator page lists these rates for the next two cycles.

  • Residential, school districts: 7.05% in 2025 and 2026.
  • Residential, local government: 6.25% in 2025 and 6.8% in 2026.
  • For 2026, the local government calculation first subtracts 10% of the first $700,000 of actual value.

The county's worked example is an $800,000 home with a school levy of 30 mills and a local levy of 65 mills. It comes to $4,942 for 2025 and $4,919 for 2026, before senior exemptions. Your own bill depends on the districts that cover your address, so use the Treasurer's lookup.

How do you appeal a Boulder property value?

You file with the Assessor between May 1 and June 8, and the county says deadlines are strictly enforced. Filing options are email, mail, fax, an online portal, a drop box in Boulder, Lafayette or Longmont, or in person at 1325 Pearl St.

Bring comparable sales and any record errors. The comparison period for the current cycle is July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2024. The Assessor mails a Notice of Determination by August 15, and you can then appeal in writing to the Board of Equalization on or before September 15.

You cannot appeal the tax itself through the Assessor, since levies are set by budgeting bodies such as city councils, school boards and special districts.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What if you owe tax and the lien goes to sale?

Boulder County sells liens on unpaid real property tax at an annual auction. The county's page lists the 2026 sale for November 13, and liens sold in 2026 carry 13% a year.

The Treasurer updates its list of advertised properties each Friday. Mobile home taxes are struck off to the county instead of being auctioned. Colorado's assessment calendar says the general tax lien attaches on January 1, so the year's tax is a live item at a closing.

What do Boulder rental rules mean if you own a rental?

Every Boulder rental needs a city license, and a sale resets the paperwork. The city says a rental inspection and a new license application are needed when ownership changes.

  • The rental license fee is $190, and inspections are done by private licensed inspectors who set their own prices.
  • Long-term rentals must hold SmartRegs energy certification before the license application is submitted.
  • Owners who live outside Boulder County must name a local agent who can reach the property within 60 minutes.
  • Short-term rentals must be the owner's principal residence, last no more than 29 days, and the license is no longer valid if the property is sold.

A buyer who purchases a rental as-is takes on the licensing step, so a cash buyer is a practical fit for landlords who want out.

What happens at closing when you sell a Boulder house?

The seller's side usually sees three items: the unpaid property tax, the county's documentary fee, and the recording fee. Colorado's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration over $500, set by C.R.S. 39-13-102 and collected by the county clerk and recorder.

Boulder County's recording fee is $43 per document as of July 1, 2025, and its clerk's office is at 1750 33rd St., Suite 201. If you owe back tax, the title company pays it from your proceeds and shows the figure on the settlement statement. Ask for that figure early so a surprise does not delay the closing.

Frequently asked questions

When is Boulder property tax due in 2026?

The Boulder County Treasurer lists March 2 and June 15 for two half payments, or April 30 for one full payment. Late interest starts the day after each due date and climbs each month.

Does the City of Boulder collect property tax?

No. The Boulder County Treasurer bills and collects it for every taxing body, and the county Assessor sets the value.

Can I sell my Boulder house if I owe property tax?

Yes. The title company normally pays the balance from your sale proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer at 303-441-3520 before you set a closing date.

What is the last day to appeal my Boulder valuation?

June 8 for the Assessor, with the postmark or submission due by 11:59 p.m. that day. A written Board of Equalization appeal follows on or before September 15 if you disagree with the determination.

Do I need a rental license to sell a Boulder rental?

You do not need one to sell, but the next owner must apply for a new license and pass an inspection. A short-term rental license ends when the property is sold.

Cash Home Buyers in Colorado

  • Colorado Springs, CO Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Where is Colorado Springs, and why does it matter for property tax?

Colorado Springs is the county seat of El Paso County, in east-central Colorado near the base of Pikes Peak, about 70 miles south of Denver. Its elevation at roughly 6,011 feet and its area at 195.761 square miles, which makes it the largest municipality in Colorado by area.

The size has a tax effect. A house on the western edge near the foothills and one in a newer subdivision on the far east side can sit in different school, fire and metro districts, so their bills differ even when the values match. The Colorado Springs Company laid out the town in 1871, and it was incorporated on June 19, 1886, so the housing stock ranges from historic districts to recent construction.

What does the City of Colorado Springs charge in property tax?

The city's own levy for tax year 2025, billed in 2026, is 3.009 mills, down 0.545 from 3.554 the year before. That figure comes from the El Paso County Treasurer's published mill levy table, and it is only one line on a bill.

The Treasurer explains that one mill equals $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, and that the total comes from applying all levies from counties, cities, school districts and special districts. The city does not mail its own bill, because El Paso County bills and collects for every taxing body in the county.

Taxing entity (El Paso County table)Tax year 2024 (billed 2025)Tax year 2025 (billed 2026)
City of Colorado Springs3.5543.009
El Paso County6.9856.857
Pikes Peak Library District3.1402.938
Colorado Springs Downtown Development Authority55

Which school district levies apply around Colorado Springs?

School levies are the largest single piece of most bills, and they vary by district. The Treasurer's table lists the following for tax year 2025.

School districtMills, tax year 2025
Colorado Springs School District 1137.695
Harrison School District 239.989
Academy School District 2045.459
El Paso County School District 4945.649
Widefield School District 357.682
Fountain-Fort Carson School District 829.765

The state's Division of Property Taxation says school districts calculate their rates separately from local governments, and its 2026 residential assessment rate for schools is 7.05%. Your tax statement shows which district applies to the parcel, so check that line before comparing two houses.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What other districts can appear on a Colorado Springs bill?

Fire, improvement and metro districts can add to the total. The Treasurer's table lists many, and the examples below show the range.

  • Broadmoor Fire Protection District: 4.5 mills for tax year 2025.
  • Black Forest Fire Protection District: 15.65 mills.
  • Old Colorado City Security and Maintenance District: 13.416 mills.
  • Banning Lewis Ranch Metro District No. 2: 46.469 mills, with other districts in that area at different levels.

Metro districts finance roads, water and parks in newer subdivisions, and the levies listed for them run far higher than for city or county services. A seller in a metro district can read the district line on the tax statement to see what it adds.

What are the Colorado Springs property tax dates for the year?

The El Paso County Treasurer publishes a full calendar, and the dates below come from it. Weekend or holiday due dates roll to the next business day.

DateWhat happens
January 10Assessor certifies the prior year's tax warrant to the Treasurer
January 28Tax statements must be mailed
Last day of FebruaryFirst-half payment due
March 31Senior tax deferral applications due to the State Treasurer
April 30Full-year payment due
June 15Second-half payment due; unpaid taxes then become delinquent
JulyDelinquent notices are mailed and interest applies
SeptemberDelinquent real estate taxes are advertised for public auction
After September 30Cash or certified funds only
OctoberDelinquent real estate taxes are sold at public auction

For 2026 the Treasurer's notice sets registration for September 30, 2026 and the sale for October 28, 2026, held electronically through RealAuction. Interest on late payments is 1% per month with no grace period and no partial payments.

How can I pay a Colorado Springs property tax bill?

You can pay online, in person or by mail, and the method affects timing. The Treasurer lists these options.

  • Online: current-year taxes through the Property Tax Search and Payment Portal by credit, debit or ACH.
  • In person: by credit or debit card at the office, with card processing fees passed to the cardholder.
  • Mail: a USPS postmark on or before the due date counts for current-year payments. On-site postage metering does not.
  • Fixed income: owners can enroll in monthly payments through EscrowTaxes.
  • Tax liens and redemptions: cash, cashier's check or money order, and postmarks are not accepted.

Card payments for current-year taxes stop being accepted after September 30. If a mortgage company pays the bill, the Treasurer advises owners to confirm with the lender whether taxes are held in escrow, because statements go to the owner of record rather than the lender.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How do I challenge a Colorado Springs assessment?

You contact the El Paso County Assessor first, then the Board of Equalization. The Assessor's office is at 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2300, phone (719) 520-6600, and it encourages an informal call before a formal appeal.

For 2026 the Clerk to the Board of Equalization, at the same address in Suite 2201, set a real property protest date of July 15, with hearings running July 6 through August 5 by Teams. Each side gets 10 minutes, the owner must prove the value, and the written decision comes within five business days. The Board's number is (719) 520-6430.

  • Evidence must rest on market data from January 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 for the 2025 and 2026 values.
  • An appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals, district court or arbitration must be filed within 30 days of the decision.
  • The district court option goes through the Fourth Judicial District Court at 270 S. Tejon Street.

Binding arbitration, available through the county, is final and cannot be reviewed.

Is there a senior property tax break in El Paso County?

Yes, if state funding is available. The El Paso County Assessor says the exemption removes up to 50% of the first $200,000 of a primary residence's value, and that the General Assembly reinstated funding for tax year 2026, payable in 2027.

A first-time applicant must be 65 or older on January 1, and must have been owner of record and lived in the house for at least 10 consecutive years. Surviving spouses have a separate path. The page gives a July 15 deadline for tax year 2026 but also says the window has closed, so call (719) 520-6600 to confirm what applies to your case. The Division of Property Taxation also describes a senior deferral, which becomes repayable when the home is sold.

How do wildfire and weather affect Colorado Springs sellers?

The city sits at the foot of the Rockies, and its largest recent wildfire reached homes inside the city. The Waldo Canyon Fire began June 23, 2012 about 4 miles northwest of the city, destroyed 347 homes, killed two people within the city and forced about 32,000 residents to evacuate.

The climate is semi-arid, with about 243 sunny days a year, around 16.5 inches of precipitation and about 38 inches of snow a season, with March the snowiest month. Roofs, insulation and defensible space therefore shape a buyer's view of a Colorado Springs house. Owners near the western hills may want to confirm their insurance and defensible space before listing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What drives the Colorado Springs housing market?

The economy rests mainly on the military, high technology and tourism, in that order. Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases, Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station, U.S. Space Command, Fort Carson and the Air Force Academy as military installations here.

Interstate 25 runs through the city for nearly 18 miles, and the second-largest commercial airport in Colorado, Colorado Springs Airport, has operated since 1925. Neighborhoods named by Wikipedia include Old Colorado City, Ivywild, the Old North End, Broadmoor and Banning Lewis Ranch.

Owners who are moving for work or are behind on a bill can ask about an as-is sale, and the title company can tell them what El Paso County tax is owed before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Who bills property tax in Colorado Springs?

The El Paso County Treasurer. The city sets a levy of 3.009 mills for tax year 2025, but the county mails the statement and collects for all taxing districts.

What is the interest rate on late Colorado Springs property tax?

The El Paso County Treasurer says late payments accrue 1% interest per month, with no grace period. Partial payments are not allowed.

When does Colorado Springs sell delinquent tax liens?

The 2026 sale is scheduled for October 28, 2026, electronically through RealAuction, with registration opening September 30, 2026.

Where do I file a Colorado Springs property tax appeal?

Start with the El Paso County Assessor at 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2300, or the Property Record Search page. The next step is the Board of Equalization, which set a July 15, 2026 protest date for real property.

What happens to a Colorado Springs tax deferral when I sell?

Repayment is required when the property is sold or title transfers. The deferral is a loan from the state treasurer recorded as a lien, with interest accruing from May 1.

What is Broomfield, and who handles its property tax?

Broomfield is a consolidated city and county between Denver and Boulder along US 36 and US 287. Because it is both, the City and County of Broomfield runs its own Assessor, Treasurer and Clerk and Recorder under one roof at One DesCombes Drive.

That makes Broomfield different from most Colorado places, where a county office bills for the cities inside it. Here a single government assesses the value, sends the bill and records the deed.

The Treasurer's number is 303-464-5810, and the Assessor is at 303-464-5819 or assessor@broomfield.org.

How did Broomfield become a city and county?

Broomfield was incorporated as a city on June 6, 1961, in the southeast corner of Boulder County, and became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001. A 1998 constitutional amendment made the new county possible.

By the 1990s the city had annexed land in Adams, Jefferson and Weld counties as well, so it was built from four counties. The name comes from broomcorn, a sorghum grown in the area, and the post office opened on September 26, 1884. The Denver-Boulder Turnpike opened January 19, 1952 and became free on September 14, 1967.

For sellers, the 2001 date matters. Broomfield's online recording portal covers documents recorded from November 2001, and older records may sit with Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld.

What do Census figures show for Broomfield housing?

Roughly 63% of Broomfield homes are owner-occupied. These are the Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures for the county, which is the same boundary as the city.

MeasureBroomfield
Population, 2020 Census74,112

Broomfield is the smallest county in Colorado by area and the fifth smallest in the country, with 2,248 people per square mile.

Who are the major employers in Broomfield?

Oracle America leads the list with 1,650 employees, according to a 2023 employer list. The five largest are shown below.

  • Oracle America: 1,650
  • Intermountain Health Care: 1,550
  • BAE Systems: 1,100
  • Hunter Douglas Window Fashions Division: 950
  • City and County of Broomfield: 900

Crocs, Vail Resorts and Webroot also have headquarters in the city.

What is Broomfield's climate, and how does it affect a house?

Broomfield has a cold semi-arid climate, with about 16 inches of precipitation a year. It sits in USDA hardiness zone 6a.

The mean daily high is 88.7 degrees in July and 45.4 in January, and the mean low is 57.6 in July and 18.3 in January. A house here goes through large swings between hot summers and cold winter nights.

Those swings are hard on roofs, exterior paint and heating systems. The 2021 Marshall Fire put parts of Broomfield under pre-evacuation orders, though the fire's destruction was in Superior, Louisville and unincorporated Boulder County.

What schools and roads serve Broomfield?

Six school districts reach into Broomfield, and the city was assembled from parts of four counties. They are listed below.

  • Boulder Valley School District
  • 27J Schools
  • Weld County School District RE-8
  • Jefferson County Public Schools
  • St. Vrain Valley School District
  • Adams 12 Five Star Schools

Your address decides which district's mill levy applies, so two houses a mile apart can see different bills. US 36 and US 287 run through the city, and Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport is nearby.

When is Broomfield property tax due?

Broomfield's Treasurer lists February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half, and April 30 for a full payment. No interest accrues if you pay by those dates.

Tax notices go to the owner of record, not the mortgage company, around the third week of January, by email or mail. If your lender pays from escrow, check with them. Taxes under $25 must use the full-tax option.

Payment optionDueLate interest starts
First halfFebruary 281% in March, rising to 10% in December
Second halfJune 151% in late June, rising to 7% in December
Full paymentApril 301% in May, rising to 8% in December

After a due date, call 303-438-6390 for updated figures.

How can you pay Broomfield property tax?

You can pay in cash, by check, by eCheck or by credit card. The credit card provider charges 2.50%, and an eCheck costs $2.50. Online payments are capped at $1,000,000 per transaction.

The office is in the George Di Ciero City and County Building at One DesCombes Drive. The Treasurer's page also mentions a senior tax deferral program, with the application at colorado.propertytaxdeferral.com. A Certificate of Taxes Due, governed by C.R.S. 39-10-115, confirms that all taxes are paid except those listed as still due.

How are Broomfield values set?

Broomfield reappraises in odd-numbered years and carries values forward in even years unless something changes. The assessment date is January 1 each year.

For the 2025 and 2026 reappraisals, residential sales from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024 are used. Only qualified arms-length sales count. The Assessor uses the market approach for homes, and its appraisers are licensed by Colorado and follow USPAP guidelines.

In an even year, a notice goes out only if something changed, such as a finished basement, an addition or a demolition. The page says tax is assessment rate times value times tax rate, and that the state legislature sets the rate while taxing authorities set the mill levy.

How do you protest a Broomfield valuation?

File with the Assessor between May 1 and June 8 for real property. Personal property protests are due by June 30.

  • Online: the appeal portal at appeals.spatialest.com/co-broomfield, which includes a neighborhood sales map and document uploads.
  • Mail: the Real Property Protest Form, postmarked by June 8, to PO Box 1149, Broomfield, CO 80038-1149.
  • In person: the Community Assistance Center in the main lobby of the City and County Building.

Useful evidence includes an appraisal dated 7/1/2022 to 6/30/2024, photos of condition, comparable sales and proof of record errors. A Notice of Determination is sent by June 30 for real property.

If you disagree, you can go to the Board of Equalization, whose deadlines are July 15 for real property and July 20 for personal property. Hearings are held remotely, run by an independent hearing officer, and you carry the burden of showing your value is more accurate. Evidence files must be 20 MB or smaller. The board's contact is clk-boe@broomfield.org or 303-438-6332, option 9. The Assessor's valuation page lists hearings in late July and a finish by August 5.

What does recording a deed cost in Broomfield?

Broomfield's schedule effective June 1, 2026 sets a flat $43 for the first page of a recorded document, with no charge for added pages. The city's recording page describes it as a $40 fee plus a $3 surcharge per document.

The documentary fee is $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500, so a $500,000 transfer pays $50. Treasurer's, public trustee's and sheriff's deeds are exempt. The Recording Division is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and documents can be mailed, dropped off, brought in or e-recorded.

Documents need a one-inch top and bottom margin and half-inch side margins, a return address and a signed check payable to the City and County of Broomfield. The office cannot give legal advice on which document to file.

What happens when you sell a Broomfield house with tax due?

The title company pays any unpaid property tax from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for current figures before you set a date, because interest grows monthly.

Broomfield's first half is due in February, a few days earlier than Boulder County's March 2. A seller who closes in late winter should confirm whether that first half has been paid.

Frequently asked questions

When are Broomfield property taxes due?

The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15, and a full payment April 30. Interest starts at 1% the month after a missed date.

Does Broomfield have a separate county government?

Yes. Broomfield became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001, so one government assesses, bills and records.

What is the deadline to protest a Broomfield valuation?

June 8 for real property. Appeals to the Board of Equalization follow, with a July 15 deadline for real property.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Broomfield?

The flat recording fee is $43 per document under the schedule effective June 1, 2026. Add the documentary fee of $0.01 per $100 over $500.

Can I sell a Broomfield house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. Closing agents pay the balance from the sale proceeds. Call the Treasurer at 303-464-5810 or 303-438-6390 for the exact amount.

Where is Fort Collins, and how is it laid out?

Fort Collins is a home rule city and the seat of Larimer County, about 60 miles north of Denver and 45 miles south of Cheyenne, Wyoming. It sits at the base of the northern Front Range foothills along the Cache la Poudre River, with Spring Creek also running through town.

The city covers 58.5 square miles, stands near 5,000 feet in elevation and had 169,810 residents in the 2020 Census, making it the fourth most populous city in Colorado. Horsetooth Reservoir and Horsetooth Mountain mark the western skyline. The historic Old Town district sits next to the site of the original 1864 army post, and the city grew south from there through the late twentieth century.

Fort Collins uses a council-manager form of government. A mayor presides over a seven-member council, and six members are elected from districts.

Which office bills property tax for a Fort Collins home?

The city does not bill property tax. The Larimer County Treasurer mails the statements, collects the money and sends it to every taxing authority, including the school district, the city and special districts. The Treasurer's page is clear that the office does not decide how much tax is owed.

  • For the value of the property or how the tax was calculated, contact the Larimer County Assessor.
  • For payments, statements, delinquent balances and the lien sale, contact the Treasurer and Public Trustee, currently Irene Josey.
  • For help after a mortgage payoff, the Treasurer's site has a page on getting your tax statement once the lender no longer pays it.

The Public Trustee side of the office handles foreclosures and releases of deeds of trust, which follow Title 38 of the Colorado Revised Statutes.

What are the 2026 Larimer County tax due dates?

The Treasurer lists the first half due February 28, 2026, the second half due June 15, 2026, or a single full payment due April 30, 2026. Dates that land on a non-business day move to the next business day.

ItemLarimer County Treasurer
First halfFebruary 28, 2026
Full payment optionApril 30, 2026
Second halfJune 15, 2026
Payment styleTwo equal installments or one full payment; partial payments are not accepted
When tax becomes dueJanuary 1, for the previous year
2026 tax lien saleThursday, November 19, 2026, 8:00 a.m.

Because Larimer County says taxes become due on January 1 for the previous year, a seller closing mid-year should ask the closing company how the current year's share is handled.

Where is the Larimer County tax lien sale held?

The 2026 annual tax lien sale is scheduled for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch, 5280 Arena Circle, Loveland, in the Thomas McKee 4-H Community Building.

Fort Collins owners who still carry delinquent real estate tax should check with the Treasurer before that date. The Treasurer's site also lists information for tax lien investors, which is the other side of the same sale.

The site also posts a notice about courtesy orange tag notices for manufactured homes, which the office said it would post through September.

What payment tools does the Larimer County Treasurer offer?

The Treasurer offers online payment, receipts, eNotices and email reminders, and it has registered with EquaPay by Autoagent, formerly EscrowTaxes, for automated monthly payments. EquaPay is open to any Larimer County property that does not have taxes escrowed through a mortgage.

  • Title companies have a separate CTD login for Certificates of Taxes Due.
  • Mortgage companies have a mass payment option.
  • Owners can change their mailing address, search property and tax records, and print a receipt on the site.
  • Manufactured homes, personal property for businesses, and special assessments each have their own pages.

until about 2:00 p.m., a reminder that payment and search pages are not always available.

What does the climate mean for a Fort Collins house?

Fort Collins has a cold semi-arid climate, with about 15.88 inches of precipitation and 51.4 inches of snow in a typical year. The average temperature in December, the coldest month, is 31.1 degrees Fahrenheit, and snow can fall from early September through the end of May.

July is the warmest month, with a mean daily high of 87.4 degrees, and the record low is minus 41.

Flooding has a documented history. In late July 1997, a 31-hour storm dropped 10 to 14 inches of rain, the heaviest on record for an urban area of Colorado. Five people died, the city took about $5 million in damage, and Colorado State University's library flooded. A house near the Poudre River or Spring Creek may carry flood-related questions from buyers or lenders.

Who are the biggest employers around Fort Collins?

Colorado State University is the largest employer in Fort Collins, ahead of the University of Colorado Hospital Authority and the Poudre School District. The city's 2024 annual financial report lists the following.

EmployerEmployees

Other industries include clean energy, bioscience and agri-tech, and the city has more than 20 breweries, including New Belgium and Odell. Federal agencies based in Fort Collins, including some USDA offices, employed over 5,000 people across Colorado as of 2025.

What schools, parks and libraries serve Fort Collins neighborhoods?

Public K to 12 schools in Fort Collins belong to the Poudre School District, which runs four comprehensive high schools: Fort Collins, Rocky Mountain, Poudre and Fossil Ridge. It also lists ten middle schools and 32 elementary schools.

The city has 875 acres of developed parks, including six community parks: City Park, Edora, Fossil Creek, Lee Martinez, Rolland Moore and Spring Canyon. The Poudre River Public Library District runs branches in Old Town, Harmony and Council Tree.

The school district is one of the taxing authorities on a Fort Collins bill, so which school boundary a house sits in is part of its tax area.

What is Larimer County, which taxes Fort Collins homes?

Larimer County covers 2,634 square miles along the Wyoming border, with 359,066 residents in 2020 and a 2025 estimate of 377,292. It was created November 1, 1861 and borders Weld, Boulder, Grand and Jackson counties in Colorado and Albany and Laramie counties in Wyoming.

Fort Collins and Loveland are the two cities, and the towns include Berthoud, Estes Park, Johnstown, Timnath, Wellington and Windsor. The census counted 158,769 housing units in the county, with 63.8% of occupied units owner-occupied and 36.2% rented. Interstate 25 and U.S. 34, 36, 87 and 287 cross the county.

Public schools in Fort Collins belong to the Poudre School District, which also serves Wellington, Timnath, Windsor, Laporte and Livermore.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay property tax to in Fort Collins?

You pay the Larimer County Treasurer, not the city. The Treasurer collects for the school district, the city, the county and special districts.

When is the Larimer County tax lien sale in 2026?

It is scheduled for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch in Loveland.

Can I pay Fort Collins property tax in installments?

Yes. The Treasurer accepts two equal installments or one full payment, and does not accept partial payments. Owners without escrow can also enroll in EquaPay for monthly payments.

Which office do I call if I disagree with my value?

Call the Larimer County Assessor. The Treasurer states it does not determine the amount of tax and sends value questions to the Assessor.

How do I get a Certificate of Taxes Due in Larimer County?

Title companies use the Treasurer's CTD login, so ask your closing company to order it.

Can I sell a Fort Collins house that has tax due?

Yes. Any tax owed would be addressed at closing through the title company. If the account is delinquent, check with the Treasurer before the November lien sale.
